issues.body:
From the 2026-08-14 playtest. Pip's impression was that **departures only ever happen
*to* the player** -- attrition, poaching, resignation -- and that there is no way to let
someone go.

**The impression is wrong about the code and right about the game.** A complete,
functional fire path ships today. He could not find it, and once found, it does not behave
like the rest of the staff system. Both halves are the issue.

---

## The path exists, end to end

| Step | File:line |
|---|---|
| HUD side-button `" Employees -- roster & morale"` | `godot/scripts/ui/main_ui.gd:292-302` |
| Handler -> TabManager | `main_ui.gd:1084-1089` |
| `show_employee_screen()` swaps MainUI out | `godot/scripts/ui/tab_manager.gd:45-50` |
| Per-researcher `"Fire"` button on each card | `godot/scripts/ui/employee_screen.gd:370-381` |
| Severance `salary/12 + min(turns_employed, 8) * (salary/52)` | `employee_screen.gd:36-47` |
| Confirmation dialog, title `"Confirm Termination"` | `employee_screen.gd:26-34, 49-69` |
| `GameManager.fire_researcher()` -- validate, debit, remove | `godot/scripts/game_manager.gd:361-405` |

It is live code, not a stub: `turns_employed` is serialized (`researcher.gd:793`) and
incremented every turn (`:500`), so the tenure bonus really applies.

## Why he could not find it

- It is on the **legacy Employee screen**, reachable only through one unlabelled-ish HUD
  side-button, not from the hiring pipeline.
- The keyboard shortcut that used to open that screen is **commented out**, in two places:
  `tab_manager.gd:23-28` and `main_ui.gd:1079-1082`.
- **`HiringPanelController` has no fire affordance whatsoever.** Grep for `fire` in
  `hiring_panel_controller.gd`, `employee_panel.gd`, `staff_perks_panel.gd`: no matches.
  The screen a player associates with staffing can source, interview, offer and onboard --
  and cannot end anything.

**This is a discoverability defect that reads to the player as a missing mechanic, which
is a strictly worse failure than a missing mechanic.** A player who believes they cannot
fire anyone plans a different game.

## The half that is a genuine gap: firing has no consequences

`fire_researcher` (`game_manager.gd:361-405`) is a bare `remove_researcher()` plus a cash
deduction. Compared against **every other** way a person leaves, it omits all of it:

| | Attrition (`hiring_pipeline.gd:773-788`) | Fire (`game_manager.gd:361-405`) |
|---|---|---|
| `transition_hire_state(DEPARTED)` | yes, `:784` | **no -- the object leaves the array still flagged `EMPLOYED`** |
| Ledger entry | yes, `Ledger.staff_rider()` `:787` | **none** |
| Loyalty hit on remaining staff | -- | **none** |
| Reputation / doom | -- | **none** |
| `_format_departure()` log line (who left, new team size) | yes, `events.gd:459-465` | **bypassed entirely** |

So firing is **free** -- morally and mechanically. It also frees a desk with no penalty
(`office.gd:91-97`), which makes it a legal way to dodge the office hire cap: hire past a
tier boundary is refused, but fire-then-hire is not.

This is directly contrary to ADR-0003, which already rules on it:

> **Staff ride on this system:** staff are AP-leverage with liability riders (ADR-0008) --
> **a disgruntled ex-researcher is a secret entry**, a whistleblower is an exposure event,
> a manager is insurance that shortens fuses on people-liabilities.
> -- `docs/game-design/decisions/ADR-0003-liability-ledger.md:54-56`

Firing is the canonical way to manufacture a disgruntled ex-researcher, and it is the one
departure that mints nothing.

## Full census of how a person leaves the roster

For the record, since the claim under test was "only attrition, poaching, resignation":

| # | Mechanism | Code | Player-initiated? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fire with severance | `game_manager.gd:361-405` <- `employee_screen.gd:87` | **yes, fully** |
| 2 | Early attrition (un-mentored hire quits, 15%/month) | `hiring_pipeline.gd:773-788` | partly -- the player armed it by skipping mentoring; the roll is RNG |
| 3 | Event poach (`lose_researcher`) | `events.gd:341-350`, `_poach_least_loyal` `:427-447` | depends on the option chosen |
| 4 | Event staffing delta (negative `safety_researchers` etc.) | `events.gd:355-358, 377-403` | depends on the option chosen |
| 5 | Risk-pool resignation | `turn_manager.gd:800-803` | **no** -- fires automatically |

There is no low-loyalty resignation tick, no retirement, no death, no burnout exit.
`loyalty_hit` (`events.gd:405-421`) removes nobody.

In the event data, the closest thing to a player firing someone is
`rival_poaching` -> **"Let Them Go"** (`-1 safety_researcher, +$20,000`,
`core_events.json:281-289`) and `researcher_poached` -> "Let Them Leave"
(`core_events.json:1093-1100`). **Both are framed as declining to counter a rival, not as
dismissal.** No event anywhere has an option whose fiction is "fire this person".
(`"Dismiss Concerns"`, `core_events.json:573`, dismisses complaints, not staff.)

## What a fix should decide

1. **Where the button lives.** Either the hiring panel grows a roster tab, or the Employee
   screen gets a real route from it. Restoring the commented-out shortcut is the cheap
   half and does not fix the association problem.
2. **What firing costs beyond cash** -- loyalty on the remaining team at minimum, and per
   ADR-0003, a ledger entry. The severance formula is already the good part; the rest of
   the transaction is missing.
3. **`transition_hire_state(DEPARTED)` on the way out**, so a fired person is the same kind
   of object as an attrited one. This is a one-line correctness fix and should not wait for
   the design half.
4. **The desk-cap dodge** -- decide whether fire-then-hire past a tier boundary is intended.

## Related

- `#1004` -- parked upgrade-backed mechanics including chairs attrition; same lane.
- `#648` -- poaching rate check; the other side of this ledger.
- `docs/game-design/PEOPLE_AND_MONEY_COHESION.md` -- already names this exact gap: *"can
  fire someone and never see the severance land on a finance screen"*.

issues.title: Hiring pipeline: five things the sim knows and the panel never says -- five faces for six candidates, free offer retries, an invisible ad campaign, empty counter-offers, and the onboarding bill you only see after you commit

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
From the 2026-08-14 playtest. Five separate complaints from Pip, filed as one issue
because they are the same defect wearing five hats: **the hiring pipeline models more
state than it shows, and the state it hides is exactly the state a player needs to make
the next decision.** Every fix lands in `godot/scripts/core/hiring_pipeline.gd` and
`godot/scripts/ui/hiring_panel_controller.gd`.

Not a duplicate of `#1219` (the refusal never reaches a visible surface) or `#1218`
(costs not disclosed). Everything below is about **outcomes and history** -- what
happened, what is still happening, and what it will cost later.

---

## 1. The pool of six can only ever show five faces

Pip asked for many more portraits, "a systematic persona run". The measured state makes
that stronger than a wishlist:

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Identity slots a researcher can be minted with (`researcher.gd:101`, `IDENTITY_POOL_SIZE`) | **24** |
| Portraits wired into the game (`portrait_library.gd:19-25`, `PORTRAIT_STEMS`) | **5** |
| Distinct portraits already generated and sitting in the repo | **34** |
| Max simultaneous candidates (`game_state.gd:172`, `MAX_CANDIDATES`) | **6** |

`_index_for()` (`portrait_library.gd:62-73`) is a bare `int(NN) % 5` over the 24 slots,
with no roster awareness. **By pigeonhole, a full candidate pool is guaranteed to contain
a duplicate face**, and the four founding candidates collide often. There is no
de-duplication and no placeholder path -- a missing file just renders the card text-only
(`:39-51`).

The art is not the blocker. On disk, unwired:

- `art_generated/researcher_portraits_pilot/v1/` -- 24 distinct portraits (2 style poles x
  6 archetypes x 2 versions), including a sixth archetype `fresh_grad_believer` that was
  never staged.
- `art_generated/round3_rerolls/v1/` -- 10 distinct portraits, prompts hardened against
  anime drift, deliberately varying gender and ethnicity per archetype.

The generation pipeline is also already built and schema'd:
`art_prompts/researcher_portraits_pilot.yaml` and `art_prompts/round3_rerolls.yaml` carry
`schema_version`, style poles, per-asset `prompt_tail` persona text, and a
`generation_history` with model, prompt hash and `cost_usd: 0.06` per image. **A systematic
persona run is a config file and a promotion pass, not a new capability** -- the same
shape as the share/promote route in `#1166`.

Two more facts for whoever picks it up:
- Only the `_256` variant is ever loaded (`portrait_library.gd:14`); the 512 and 1024 PNGs
  are dead weight in the `.pck`. See `#787` for why that matters.
- `godot/assets/portraits/README.md` describes the intended system as *"per-archetype
  variant pools with random assignment"* -- unbuilt -- and still claims the portraits are
  *"STAGED-BUT-UNWIRED. No UI slot references these yet"*, which is stale.
- The floor-sprite pool (`worker_variant_pool.gd`, 5 variants) indexes `appearance_id`
  **independently** of the portrait pool, so a person's card face and their office sprite
  are uncorrelated. Same person, two unrelated appearances.

## 2. A rejected offer leaves no mark, so the same lowball can be sent forever

Pip reported that repeated offers to the same candidate fail silently. The truth is worse
than silent failure: **the second offer is not a failure at all, it is a free retry.**

There is a guard against a *concurrent* second offer and it works cleanly --
`hiring_pipeline.gd:285-286` refuses with `"%s already has an offer out."`, spends nothing,
and the button is disabled with a matching tooltip (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:250-255`).

**There is no guard, and no memory, once the first offer resolves.** Grep for
`already_offered` / `offers_made` / `offer_count` across `godot/**/*.gd`: zero hits.
`Researcher` carries no offer history; the only lifecycle field is `HireState`, and a
rejection returns the candidate to `CANDIDATE_IN_POOL` (`hiring_pipeline.gd:317`)
**unchanged** -- same `self_worth_floor`, same appetites, no resentment, no reputation
cost, no recollection.

`_resolve_offer` (`:304-321`) rejects with probability
`clampf(shortfall_frac * 2.0, 0.0, 1.0)`. So **any offer with `shortfall_frac < 0.5` is a
guaranteed eventual hire** by re-sending the identical lowball every 2 workdays at 1
Attention, until the roll finally lands -- as a `resentful_accept` (-15 loyalty, one
`Ledger.resentment_debt`). The negotiation read, the self-worth floor and the resentment
mechanic are all real; retry defeats all three.

**And the rejection itself is never told to the player.** `_resolve_offer` produces an
`offer_rejected` event at `:318`; grep for `offer_rejected` outside `hiring_pipeline.gd`
returns **zero consumers**. This is the same shape as `#1219` but on the resolution path
rather than the queue path -- fixing `#1219` will not surface it.

Two adjacent holes in the same function:
- `make_offer` checks only `KIND_OFFER`, not `KIND_INTERVIEW`. Offering during an in-flight
  interview is allowed; on accept the candidate leaves the pool (`:329`), the orphaned
  interview job later finds `find_pool_candidate == null` (`:712-713`) and is **silently
  dropped** -- 2 Attention burned, no message.
- The Attention refund on a refused offer is a raw field poke,
  `state.month_plan.attention_spent -= cost_att` (`:292`), not an API call. Worth a look
  alongside the accounting in the Action Queue issue.

**Also worth ruling on:** the offer dialog seeds the SpinBox with `read["mid"]`
(`hiring_panel_controller.gd:497`). With a recruiter `mid == floor` exactly (`:266`);
without one, `mid == salary_expectation >= floor`. Since acceptance is `cash >= floor`
(`:309`), **clicking "Send Offer" without touching the number is a guaranteed clean accept
in both cases.** The negotiation only exists if the player chooses to make it exist.

## 3. Advertise: $8,000 and 3 Attention buy an invisible thing

Pip: *"if a candidate joins the pool, that would be cool."* What actually happens:

`advertise` (`hiring_pipeline.gd:107-127`) costs **$8,000 + 3 Attention**, grants +1
reputation immediately, and adds **nothing to the pool**. It appends a campaign
(`:122-126`) with `campaign_months = 3`, `per_month_min = 0`, `per_month_max = 2`.
Candidates are drawn only at month boundaries (`_tick_campaigns`, `:754-770`;
`month_controller.gd:406-410`), `randi_range(0, 2)` per month.

**Expected yield 0-6 over three months, mean 3, and a 1-in-27 chance of paying $8,000 for
literally nothing.**

What the player is told:

1. Once, on click: `"Launched a hiring ad campaign (candidates trickle in over the coming
   months)."`
2. Monthly, **only on a hit**: `_surface_hiring_notifications` (`month_controller.gd:426-447`)
   emits one feed line per month and **returns early when `ad_hits <= 0`** -- a zero-yield
   month says nothing at all. Which is indistinguishable from the campaign having ended.
3. Nothing else, ever. `update_inflight_display` (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:569-666`)
   renders `hiring.jobs` and onboarding rows and **never reads `hiring.campaigns`.** There
   is no months-remaining indicator anywhere. See the Action Queue issue: this is also the
   3 Attention that appear in the header and in no panel.

The at-cap silent discard is **already filed** -- `#961` records that if the pool is at
`MAX_CANDIDATES = 6`, `_add_sourced_candidate` returns `false` (`:183-189`) and
`_tick_campaigns` (`:763-765`) appends no event, so *"paid campaign candidates are silently
discarded at cap"*. That issue rules that "what happens at cap must NEVER be silent". **The
finding here is the case below the cap**, which `#961` does not cover: a campaign running
normally, under the cap, is invisible from launch to first hit, and a zero-yield month is
indistinguishable from no campaign at all.

And the stale claim already noted in the legibility issue: `action_bar_renderer.gd:68-74`
greys `advertise` out as COMING SOON and its comment asserts this applies "everywhere it
renders (action bar + hiring submenu)". **It does not** -- the hiring panel's own Advertise
button (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:90-96`) is fully enabled with no such warning. One of
those two surfaces is lying, and per `#1221` we now have a convention for saying which.

## 4. Counter-offers: "low specificity" is exactly right

There is **no counter-offer mechanic in the hiring pipeline at all.** Grep for
`counter_offer|counteroffer|negotiat` across `godot/scripts` + `godot/data` returns the
`negotiation_read` docstrings and three hardcoded event options -- nothing else. What the
pipeline has is a **one-shot offer with a read**: two player-controlled parameters (a cash
SpinBox, and four promise checkboxes keyed to appetites at `hiring_pipeline.gd:71-76`),
resolved 2 workdays later as accept / resentful-accept / reject. No candidate response, no
"they want $X more", no second round.

The three things actually labelled counter-offer are all rival-retention events, all fixed
price, all anonymous:

| Event | Option | Cost | Effect | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rival_poaching` | **"Counter-Offer"** | $80,000 | **`effects: {}` -- empty** | `core_events.json:270-278` |
| `researcher_poached` | "Match Their Offer" | $50,000 | `reputation: +2` | `core_events.json:1069-1080` |
| `researcher_poached` | "Counter with Promotion" | $30,000 + 1 Attention | `reputation: +3` | `core_events.json:1081-1092` |

**No person is named** (the event fires against an anonymous "top researcher"), no amount
is chosen, and **no `Researcher.current_salary` is ever changed by any of them.** The
$80,000 option's only mechanical effect is that you did not take the other option. That is
the "low specificity" Pip felt, measured.

The pieces to fix it already exist -- `negotiation_read` (`hiring_pipeline.gd:247-269`)
gives a named band, and the appetite/promise system gives non-cash levers. A retention
counter-offer should be able to use both, against a named person.

## 5. Onboarding obligations: the Attention is previewed, the money is not

Pip wants a checklist of what a hire will require, before committing. Half of it exists,
and the ask is already on record: `#789` item 1 asks that laptop-provisioning and mentoring
*"act as predictable AP sinks you can plan for **when you make the offer**"*. **This section
is the measurement of how far short the shipped dialog falls of that.**

**The full obligation set a single hire creates:**

| Obligation | Attention | Money | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `laptop` | 1 | **$3,000** | `hiring_pipeline.gd:64`, `hiring.onboarding.laptop_money` |
| `visa` -- **only if `needs_visa`, which is `serial % 4 == 0`, i.e. 1 hire in 4** | 2 | **$5,000** | `:97-100`, `:394-395` |
| `systems` (hard-requires `laptop`) | 1 | 0 | `:65`, `:487-488` |
| `meet_people` | 1 | 0 | `:66` |
| mentoring (optional) | 2 | 0 | `:67` |
| **Total** | **3-5 Att** | **$3,000-$8,000** | |
| Until the checklist clears | | | **x0.4 output** (`researcher.gd:303-304`) |
| If mentoring is skipped | | | **x0.85 output forever** + **15% quit roll per month** (`hiring_pipeline.gd:773-788`) |
| Salary | | annual/260 **every turn** | `turn_manager.gd:139`, `clock.gd:38-44` |
| A desk, permanently | | | `office.gd:99-100`; caps 2/4/7/9 by tier, `godot/data/office/offices.json` |
| Each ticked promise | | | a real `Ledger` payable, fuse 8-12 (`ledger.gd:143-148`) |
| A below-floor accept | | | `resentment_debt` (principal 1500, fuse 6) + **-15 loyalty** |

A fully mentored onboard is **5 Attention out of ~20 for the month** -- a quarter of the
month's decision budget, per hire, and that is deliberate (`hiring_pipeline.gd:44-62`).

**What the offer dialog previews** (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:473-484`):

> If they accept: onboarding costs ~%d Attention (+%d optional mentoring). Reserve on hand: %d.

plus per-promise ledger cost text (`:520-521`), e.g. *"owes 1 first-author paper slot in
~10 turns"*. That is good, and it is the model for the rest.

**What it does not preview:**

1. **The onboarding cash.** `hard_checklist_money()` exists (`hiring_pipeline.gd:451-456`)
   and is called from `build_onboard_prompt`, `_provision_hard_checklist`, `_resolve_job`
   and tests -- **never from the offer dialog.** The dialog computes the Attention and
   omits the money on the adjacent line. The number first appears on the
   `"<name> said yes"` card (`:572-607`), where it rides `costs: {"money": money}`
   (`:596-597`) -- **after the player is committed.**
2. **The visa.** `needs_visa` is not in `get_card_data()` (`researcher.gd:707-729`) and not
   on the candidate card. A $5,000 / 2-Attention hire is indistinguishable from a $0 / 0
   one except by reading `~5` instead of `~3`.
3. **Recurring payroll.** The field is captioned `"Cash offer ($/yr):"` with no per-month
   burn and no runway-after-this-hire.
4. **Desk space.** `"desks_free"` is in `to_dict()` (`game_state.gd:1455`) and grep for
   `desks_free|hire_cap|occupied_desks` across `godot/scripts/ui` returns **zero hits**.
   The player meets the office cap only as a refusal string after clicking Send Offer.
5. **The x0.4 unproductive period** -- explained only afterwards, on the onboarding card.
6. **The 15% attrition risk** -- described as `"early-quit risk"` (`:621`), never numbered.

**And one trap worth its own line:** the mentoring prompt (`build_mentoring_prompt`,
`:610-639`) treats **lapsing or dismissing the card as choosing to skip**
(`:664-667`) -- silently arming the permanent x0.85 debuff and the 15% monthly quit roll.
A player who closes a popup has made a permanent decision and was not told so. That is a
`#1221` case: the card must say what dismissal means.

## Related

- `#789` -- hiring stitch: onboarding sub-actions as plannable sinks **at offer time**. Part
  5 is the gap report against it.
- `#1086` -- the onboard-now window tooltip omits the Attention cost and prints a raw
  `money: 3000.0`. Same $3,000 as part 5, one screen later.
- `#1091` -- every hiring route must surface the onboarding choice; no onboarded-by-silence.
  **The lapse-equals-skip trap at the end of part 5 is a live instance.**
- `#961` -- candidate pool cap; the at-cap half of part 3, already ruled.
- `#1092` -- asset sweep then bulk-generate. The closest existing container for part 1's
  persona run.
- `#793` -- office floor renders all staff as the same character. The sprite-side twin of
  part 1, and the reason to index both pools from one identity.
- `#1218` item A -- the same five hiring actions labelled "No costs" while spending 1-3
  Attention. Different defect, same five buttons.
- `#830` -- *ux(hiring): statefulness -- ask WHO, per-candidate interviews, interview popup
  w/ card+info fade-in, portraits, embedded employee panel.* The nearest existing home; part
  1 and part 2 are the measured version of its "statefulness" and "portraits" bullets.
- `#813` -- stateful candidate representation, knowledge-gated portrait to lanyard.
- `#954` -- click small pool card -> full candidate card. The natural surface for parts 1
  and 5.
- `docs/game-design/BUILD_BRIEF_HIRING_PIPELINE.md` -- already specifies most of this,
  including *"a prestige-hungry candidate takes less cash for a first-authorship promise"*
  and *"Onboard: predictable checklist (laptop, mentoring...)"*. This issue is largely a
  report that Phase B shipped its sim and not its readouts.
- `#1166` -- the promote-art route part 1 needs.

issues.title: Legibility: the hotkey badges lose to modulate, 'press 1-9' is wrong at 13 tiles, and there is no font-size SSOT to turn (378 sites)

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

labels.name: ui
labels.description: What it looks like. If pixels alone fix it, it is ui.

issues.body:
From the 2026-08-14 playtest. Filed as one issue because it is one complaint -- **you
cannot read the game** -- and because the four parts share a single root: **there is no
font-size SSOT to turn, so every legibility decision in this project has been made
locally, 378 times.**

Pip's reference point, verbatim:

> like in SCII... I never had difficulty telling what the hotkeys were

and the ask:

> the text can just all universally go up 2 to 4 points apart from maybe the player guide

He is right to exempt the guide, and for a reason he could not have known:
`player_guide.tscn:55` carries the largest font in the game (42pt title). It is also the
one screen with a *different* bug -- see part 4.

**He has already ruled on this once.** `#1140`, from the Fresh Eyes Teardown response:

> the 10-pixel hint line -- fucking terrible, let's make that like a 50-pixel hint line and
> just make all the text much bigger

That ruling has never had a ticket. This is it, with the measurements attached.

---

## 1. Hotkey badges: the number is a Button label fighting the icon for space

`godot/scripts/ui/action_bar_renderer.gd:261-275`. The hotkey is not a badge, not an
overlay, not baked art -- it is **`Button.text` on the icon tile itself**, so Godot lays
it out *beside* the icon inside a 70x70 box (`:246`) with `expand_icon = true` (`:258`).
Icon and number compete for the same 70 pixels.

```gdscript
elif action_index < 9:
    icon_button.text = str(action_index + 1)
    icon_button.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 14)  # Increased from 9
    icon_button.add_theme_color_override("font_color", Color(1, 1, 1, 1))  # Full opacity
```

The comments record that someone already fought this fight: 9 -> 14, and "full opacity".
**Both are then undone one screen down**, because `modulate` is applied to the whole
button, text included:

| Tile state | `modulate` | Effective badge colour | Line |
|---|---|---|---|
| affordable | `Color(0.9,0.9,0.9).lerp(button_color, 0.4)` | below white | `:300` |
| **unaffordable** | `Color(0.4, 0.4, 0.4)` | **40% grey on dark** | `:296` |
| coming-soon | `Color(0.35, 0.35, 0.35)` | 35% grey | `:293` |

On turn 1 most of the bar is unaffordable, so most of the numbers a new player needs are
rendered at 40% of the colour someone deliberately set to 1.0. **A `font_color` override
cannot win against a parent `modulate`.** That is the contrast bug, and it is one line of
cause, not a taste question.

## 2. "press 1-9" is wrong, key 3 does nothing, and six tiles have no key at all

The screenshot shows **13 action tiles**. The status bar says:

> Phase: SELECT ACTIONS - Click actions or press 1-9

`main_ui.gd:1404`. The claim is repeated at `main_ui.gd:358` (*"Keyboard: 1-9 for
actions"*) and in the player guide itself, `player_guide.tscn:126` (*"1-9: queue the
numbered action"*).

The cap at 9 is real and lives in three independent places:

| Cap | Where |
|---|---|
| Badge drawn only for `action_index < 9`, **with no `else`** | `action_bar_renderer.gd:270` |
| Only `action_1` .. `action_9` are ever bound (`KEY_1`..`KEY_9`) | `godot/autoload/keybind_manager.gd:72-81` |
| `_action_slot_for_event` loops `for i in range(9)` | `main_ui.gd:647-654` |

So tiles at index >= 9 get **no text at all** -- not a number, not a dash. That is the
numberless second-row icon in the screenshot, and it is not a rendering glitch; it is the
missing `else`.

**And there is a worse one inside the nine.** `advertise` sits in
`COMING_SOON_ACTION_IDS` (`action_bar_renderer.gd:73`), so it renders `"SOON"` -- **but it
still consumes index 2.** The visible badge sequence is therefore:

> `1, 2, SOON, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9`

**The number 3 never appears on the bar**, and pressing `3` routes to the disabled
`advertise` button, which `_trigger_action_by_index` silently drops
(`main_ui.gd:741`, `if button and not button.disabled`). One of the nine advertised keys
is dead, and it is dead in the way `#1219` is about: no refusal, no sound, nothing.

(Related but separate: the hiring panel's own Advertise button is *fully enabled* with a
plain tooltip -- the "coming soon" gating is only on the action bar, and
`action_bar_renderer.gd:68-74` claims in a comment that it applies "everywhere it
renders". It does not. That belongs to the hiring issue.)

**This is evidence for `#1132`'s proposed rule, not against it.** Pip's own proposal there
was to cap the top bar at ten buttons -- *"including how many buttons we want to have
unlocked in total, so we can kind of lock ourselves into a UI width"* -- i.e. bound the
design by the bar. **That cap does not exist yet, and the bar has already outgrown the
keyboard.** The two fixes are alternatives: either the hotkey scheme grows past nine, or
the action set is capped and this stops happening. Deciding which is `#1132`'s call, and
the badge/`else` bug needs fixing either way.

**The grouped/"proposed" layout draws no hotkey number at all** --
`_build_action_row()` sets `row.text = "  " + action_name` (`:402`) and never adds a
badge. Whatever is decided here has to be decided twice, or the proposed layout has to
inherit it.

## 3. No font-size SSOT: 378 sites, and the one lever that exists is dead code

Pip's "+2 to +4 points universally" is currently a **378-site mechanical edit**, because
there is nothing central to change.

**(a) Scene overrides -- the dominant mechanism.** 215 `theme_override_font_sizes/*`
declarations across 19 files in `godot/scenes/`. Nineteen distinct values:
`10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 28, 32, 36, 38, 40, 42, 48, 72`.

**(b) Runtime overrides.** 163 `add_theme_font_size_override(...)` calls across 33 files
in `godot/scripts/` and `godot/autoload/`. Range 8 to 54, and **bottom-heavy**: `10`
appears 34 times, `12` 25 times, `14` 22 times, `9` 13 times, `11` 12 times.
**Roughly 52% of all runtime-set text in the game is 12px or smaller.**

**(c) `ThemeManager` -- exists, defines a scale, is not used.**
`godot/autoload/theme_manager.gd:118-123` declares
`{"title_size": 32, "header_size": 24, "body_size": 16, "small_size": 12}`, and the
`retro` theme overrides two of them (`:219-220`). It has **exactly one caller in the
codebase** -- `notification_manager.gd:167` -- **and that call is broken**: it asks for
`"body"` while the key is `"body_size"`, so it always takes the `, 16` fallback at
`theme_manager.gd:283`. The theme scale has never scaled anything.

`music_controls.gd:31-42` documents a deliberate refusal to route through it (hand-authored
panel heights would break on a theme swap) and hard-codes its own four-value scale
instead. That refusal is reasonable and it is also the mechanism by which the SSOT stayed
empty.

**(d) `theme/menu_theme.tres` declares exactly one font size** --
`Button/font_sizes/font_size = 16` (`:161`). No Label, no RichTextLabel, no default. **And
`godot/scenes/main.tscn` has no `theme =` line at all**, so every unoverridden string on
the in-game screen -- including the phase label from part 2 -- falls back to Godot's
built-in default.

**(e) There is no accessibility text-size setting.** The settings menu's ACCESS column
(`settings_menu.tscn:459-482`) offers colourblind mode and nothing else. `project.godot:45-46`
sets `stretch/mode="canvas_items"` against 1920x1080, so text scales with the *window* and
there is no independent lever.

**The cheap version of Pip's ask is not "+3 everywhere".** It is: put a real
`default_font_size` on a shared theme, apply the theme to `main.tscn`, then delete every
override that merely restates a value. The bump becomes one number, and this issue stops
recurring.

### The worst screen, and it is the one he named -- twice

Pip asked for the hiring pipeline screen to be bigger, "possibly full-screen". He asked for
it before, in `#1041`:

> `[2:11]` The hiring pipeline screen needs to be roughly double its size -- "so we can see
> everything"

It is worse than either ask assumes. `hiring_panel_controller.gd` has **no `.tscn`** -- the whole panel is built
in code as a bare `Panel` at a hard-coded size, positioned absolutely, with no anchors:

```gdscript
var dsize := Vector2(580, 640)   # hiring_panel_controller.gd:51-56
```

That is 30% of the reference width and 59% of the height -- about **18% of screen area**,
and it does not grow with the window; on a larger display it stays 580px while everything
else scales. The "Make an Offer" sub-dialog is smaller still, `Vector2(460, 470)` (`:434-437`).

Inside those 580 pixels, the type sizes are:

| Element | Size | Line |
|---|---|---|
| panel header / subtitle | 15 / **10** | `:73`, `:81` |
| section headers | 12 | `:125`, `:146` |
| candidate card title | 12 | `:185` |
| **candidate stats** | **9** | `:190` |
| **deep-dive text** | **9** | `:199` |
| **job-lead text** | **9** | `:222` |
| every action button | 10 | `:330-367` |
| offer dialog: band / onboarding / promise header | **9** | `:469`, `:482`, `:504` |

**The densest, most decision-heavy panel in the game renders its actual decision data at
9px inside a fixed box that never grows.** If one screen leads this work, it is this one.

## 4. Player guide nested scrollbars -- CLAIM VERIFIED, still present

Pip suspected the guide *"still has its weird little triple internal scrollbars"*. He
reported it once already, in `#1141`:

> these are all scrollable little mid-sections, as opposed to one long continuous scroll,
> which is weird

and `#1140` records the standing disposition: *"Player guide is broken and known; fix
later."*

**Confirmed, still present, and "triple" is an undercount -- it is up to five.**

`godot/scenes/player_guide.tscn` is one outer `ScrollContainer` (`ContentScroll`, `:69`)
containing four `RichTextLabel`s (`:89`, `:114`, `:144`, `:175`). Every one of the four:

- has a **fixed `custom_minimum_size`** height -- `Vector2(0, 96)` `:90`, `(0, 150)` `:115`,
  `(0, 190)` `:145`, `(0, 140)` `:176`
- does **not** set `fit_content` (defaults `false`)
- does **not** set `scroll_active = false` (defaults `true`)

In Godot 4 that is the exact recipe for an internal scrollbar. At the panel's 1100px width
(`:32-35`) and 16pt body, all four blocks overflow their clamped heights -- the Resources
block is roughly 16 wrapped lines in a 190px box. **Outer scrollbar plus four inner ones.**

**This is the only screen in the codebase that does it.** Every other RichTextLabel pairs
`fit_content = true` with `scroll_active = false`: `bug_report_panel.tscn:167-168`,
`main.tscn:340-341` and `:393-394`, `whats_new_modal.tscn:105-106`,
`employee_screen.tscn:60-61` and `:87-88`, `welcome_overlay.tscn:97-98`, and in code
`plan_screen.gd:74-75`, `screen_mode.gd:65-66`, `game_over_screen.gd:753-754`,
`travel_panel_controller.gd:256-257`, `employee_screen.gd:330-331`.

**It was never fixed.** `git log -- godot/scenes/player_guide.tscn
godot/scripts/ui/player_guide.gd` returns 7 commits, none of them a scroll fix. The most
recent, `78be0370` (`#1136`), rewrote the *copy* -- which lengthened the blocks and
plausibly made the nesting worse.

**Fix: two properties per label, minus four `custom_minimum_size` clamps.** The outer
`ContentScroll` then does all the scrolling, once.

## Related

- `#1140` -- the ruling this issue implements ("make all the text much bigger"), plus
  *"Player guide is broken and known; fix later."*
- `#1141` -- Pip's first report of part 4, three weeks before this playtest.
- `#1132` -- cap the top bar at 10 buttons; the design-side alternative to part 2.
- `#1041` `[2:11]` -- the hiring panel needs "roughly double its size".
- `#936` -- attention items force the action menu to compact with inconsistent item sizes;
  same surface as parts 1-2, different pressure.
- `#953` -- large upper-right advisor text. `#794` -- bigger gantt font. Two more
  single-widget instances of the same missing scale.
- `#1011` -- three docs disagree with `keybind_manager.gd`. Part 2 adds a fourth
  disagreement, this time between the code and the game's own on-screen hint.
- `#1043` -- the Plan-screen layout brief (*"legibility, particularly legibility for new
  players... the amount of scattered text over the screen is hard to read"*). That issue
  owns **where things go**; this one owns **how big they are**. They should land in the
  same lane and not re-litigate each other.
- `#578` -- legibility pass, item (3) researcher info on the hire screen. Same panel as
  part 3.
- `#1202` -- early-game legibility, five findings. Part 2's dead `3` key is the same class
  as its item 1: a click that produces nothing at all.
- `#1130` -- action-bar wrap fix; the second row that part 2's uncapped badge logic now
  has to serve.

issues.title: The Action Queue and the Attention header contradict each other in one frame -- three widgets, three data sources, one column (and 'ticks' is a word we never defined)

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
**This answers the open design call in `#828` and supersedes it.** That issue asked, in
July, whether hiring actions being absent from the action queue was intended or an
inconsistency, and left it as a question. `#1041` `[2:21]` recorded the same observation
and Pip's answer ("wants both"). What is new here is that **the absence is now a visible
contradiction rather than an omission**, plus the traced mechanism, a second cause the
hiring fix would not touch, and the vocabulary problem underneath. `#828` should be closed
against this.

---

**One frame of the 2026-08-14 playtest contains a screen arguing with itself.** The
Action Queue says it is empty. The header, six inches above it, says eight Attention are
queued. The panel directly *below* the empty-state hint lists four jobs in flight. All
three are correct about the number they hold; none of them is reading the same number.

Screenshot `2026-08-14 15-12-12`, verbatim from the pixels:

| Surface | What it said | What it was reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top bar | `Attention: 20 (12 free, 8 queued)` | `month_plan.attention_spent` (`main_ui.gd:1176-1195`) |
| Attention gauge | `ATTENTION ********ooooooooooo  - 8/20 allocated - 0 reserved` | the same scalar (`plan_screen.gd:89-107`) |
| **Action Queue** | **`No actions queued yet -- click an action to add it here.`** | **`PlanController.queued_actions`, a UI-only mirror (`plan_controller.gd:30`)** |
| IN-FLIGHT HIRING | `Offer: Iris Wilson 0/2 ticks` (x3 + `Networking: sourcing a lead`) | `HiringPipeline.jobs` (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:570-666`) |

Three data sources, one column of the screen, no arbitration.

## Why they disagree -- the exact mechanism

`month_plan.attention_spent` has **two disjoint sets of writers, and only one of them
mints a queue tile.**

**Writer A -- mints a tile.** `GameManager.select_action()`,
`godot/scripts/game_manager.gd:274-278`: debits `attention_spent`, then appends to
`state.queued_actions`; the view mirrors it via `submenu_controller.gd:158-160` ->
`plan_controller.queue_action()`, and a tile appears.

**Writer B -- mints nothing.** `MonthPlan.spend_attention()`,
`godot/scripts/core/month_plan.gd:252-268`. Its own docstring states the intent plainly:

> Spend `cost` Attention from the AVAILABLE (un-reserved) pool at plan speed, **without
> minting a queued-strategic WIP entry**. This is the primitive the hiring pipeline (and
> other duration subsystems that track their own jobs) use: the founder currency is still
> debited here, but the duration/target bookkeeping lives in the subsystem.

Every hiring action is Writer B:

| Action | Attention | Debit site | Job recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `advertise` | 3 | `hiring_pipeline.gd:114-117` | `campaigns` (`:121-125`) -- **rendered nowhere at all** |
| `use_connections` | 2 | `:138-141` | `jobs` (`:143-150`) |
| `interview_next` | 2 | `:208-209` | `jobs` (`:211-217`) |
| `hire_best` (offer) | 1 | `:287-288` | `jobs` (`:294-300`) |
| `onboard_next` | 1-2 per hire | `:473-501`, `:533` | onboarding flags |

The hiring panel's result handler (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:398-406`) refreshes the
header and the in-flight panel and **never calls `update_queued_actions_display()`**. So
the design intent -- "the subsystem tracks its own jobs" -- is honoured in the sim and
abandoned in the UI: the founder currency moves on the shared readout while the shared
readout's neighbour insists nothing is happening.

**The screenshot's own arithmetic:** three offers (1 each) + one connections (2) = 5. The
missing 3 is almost certainly one `advertise`, which appends to `campaigns` -- a list
**neither** widget reads. So part of that 8 is invisible in *both* panels, not just the
queue.

**A second, independent cause of the same contradiction.** At commit,
`main_ui.gd:1042` and `:1070` call `plan_controller.reset_mirror()`
(`plan_controller.gd:100-106`), which empties the mirror with no refund, while
`attention_spent` persists until `MonthPlan.begin_month()` (`month_plan.gd:127-129`).
**After any commit the widget is empty by construction while the header still reports the
month's spend as "queued".** Fixing only the hiring seam leaves this one standing.

(Third, latent: `MonthPlan.queued_strategic` is rendered only by `QueueGantt`
(`queue_gantt.gd:36-49`), which is gated to the `proposed` layout at `main_ui.gd:776`.
`#1221` establishes that lane has no production writer, so it is always empty too.)

## The second half: "ticks" is not a word we have ever defined

Pip flagged `0/2 ticks` as jargon. It is worth being precise about what kind of problem
that is, because it is **not** a hidden-cost problem of the `#1218` family.

**The durations are real, declared, Balance-driven, and correct:**

| Kind | Balance key | Value | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| connections | `hiring.connections.duration_ticks` | 2 | `godot/data/balance/defaults.json:57` |
| interview | `hiring.interview.duration_ticks` | 3 | `defaults.json:58` |
| offer | `hiring.offer.duration_ticks` | 2 | `defaults.json:59` |

The UI reads the same keys with the same fallbacks (`hiring_panel_controller.gd:604-610`),
so the bars cannot drift from the sim. **Nothing is hidden. It is illegible.**

A tick is a turn is one workday -- `clock.gd:5` (`One turn = one WORKDAY`), `clock.gd:13`
(`TURNS_PER_WEEK = 5`), `clock.gd:29-32`; jobs resolve on
`state.turn + duration_ticks` (`hiring_pipeline.gd:149, 215, 298`) inside
`HiringPipeline.on_tick()` (`:692-705`), one per `MonthController.advance_tick()`.

**The word is defined nowhere a player can reach.** `grep -i tick docs/PLAYERGUIDE.md` ->
zero hits. `docs/GLOSSARY.md`'s only "tick" is a release-version example (`:110`). The
only in-game tooltip that explains it (`queue_gantt.gd:142`, *"Lands on resolution tick
(turn) %d."*) is in the proposed layout the player is not running.

**And the game already renders the identical quantity as "days" elsewhere:**

| String | Where | Word |
|---|---|---|
| `%d/%d ticks` | `hiring_panel_controller.gd:662` + `:616` | **ticks** |
| `%d/%d steps` | same line, `:637` -- onboarding | **steps** (fair: checklist items, not time) |
| `~$%d bills in %d ticks` | `finance_engine.gd:340` | **ticks** |
| `Back from %s after %d days.` (value is `ticks_resolved`) | `conference_trip.gd:383` | **days** |
| `%d days away \| %d Attention consumed` (also `ticks_resolved`) | `conference_vignette.gd:155,164` | **days** |
| `day %d -- %s %d` | `screen_mode.gd:174` | **day** |

The travel surfaces already made the right call. Hiring did not. And because `3/4 steps`
and `0/2 ticks` sit in the same list under one `IN-FLIGHT HIRING` header, they read as the
same kind of progress when one is a clock and the other is a checklist.

## What a fix has to decide

1. **One list, or one honest label.** Either the queue widget renders in-flight hiring
   (and advertising campaigns) as tiles, or the header stops calling `attention_spent`
   "queued". The current pairing is the only combination that is wrong on its face.
2. **The post-commit case** (`reset_mirror` vs. persistent `attention_spent`) must be
   handled or the contradiction survives the fix.
3. **`advertise` leaves no trace anywhere.** `campaigns` (`hiring_pipeline.gd:121`) has no
   renderer. A player who spends 3 Attention and $8,000 on it can see the money leave and
   has no surface that says a campaign is running. See the hiring issue for the rest of
   that story.
4. **Say "days".** One word, three call sites, and it is the word the rest of the game
   already uses.

## Related

- `#828` -- *hiring actions don't appear in the action queue*. **Superseded by this.** Its
  design question ("where should hiring commitments surface?") is answered by the fact that
  the header already claims they are in the queue.
- `#1041` `[2:21]` -- *"Hiring actions stack in the in-flight section but do not create
  cards in the action queue. Pip wants both."* Same observation, three weeks earlier, from
  the same person.
- `#1044` -- *actions resolve instantly, so the early game has no rhythm*. Its item 3 --
  *"the queue should promise a completion time... once actions take time, the queue stops
  being a list and becomes a schedule"* -- is the destination this widget is heading for.
  **Hiring is currently the only thing in the game that does take time**, which is why it is
  the first system to break the widget. Read before designing the fix.
- `#794` -- *PLAN operations gantt: bigger font/area + a 'what's next / ETA to land'
  indicator*. The ETA half of that ask is this widget. Whoever picks this up should read
  it first; the two should not be built twice.
- `#1037` / `#1208` / `#1209` -- the vocabulary lane. The "ticks" half of this issue is the
  same shape as those three: a term of art printed on screen and defined nowhere. `#1037`
  also records that `GLOSSARY.md` has no player-facing counterpart, which is where "day"
  would be defined once.
- `#1218` -- the hidden-Attention audit. **This is deliberately not that:** these costs are
  disclosed. The complaint is arithmetic that does not add up on screen.
- `#1219` -- silent submenu rejections, same hiring path, different failure (nothing
  queued *and* nothing said). Fixing that one makes this one more visible, not less.
- `#1043` -- the Plan-screen layout brief. This widget lives in the column that brief is
  about.

issues.title: Convention: a refusal must say whether it is a rule or a stub
issues.body:
## The observation

From the 2026-08-14 playtest. Onboarding a hire costs 3 Attention. With a full queue, one
option behaves correctly, but the other says:

> insufficient capacity to handle by cannibalising - pick another option

Pip:

> which, like, isn't strictly true?

and then the part that generalises:

> if its because we haven't built it, we should also say **[ALPHA: This behaviour is a stub, harass the developers to extend it!]**

## The principle, which is bigger than the string

**A stub that refuses in the voice of a rule teaches the player a rule that does not exist.**

"You cannot do that" and "we have not built that yet" are different statements. The first
is worldbuilding -- something the player is meant to learn, plan around, and still believe
at 1.0. The second is an apology. Conflating them is a specific kind of lie to the player,
and it is the in-game cousin of the false-claim problem this estate spent two days auditing
on the website (`docs/CLAIM_AUDIT_2026-08-06.md`).

**An alpha is allowed to be incomplete. It is not allowed to present incompleteness as design.**

## He was right about this one, and for a deeper reason than the wording

Traced, not guessed:

- `MonthPlan.pay_by_cannibalizing()` can only free Attention by cancelling entries in
  `MonthPlan.queued_strategic`.
- `queued_strategic` is written only by `MonthPlan.queue_strategic()`.
- Its sole production wrapper, `GameManager.queue_strategic_action()`, has **zero callers**.
  The only callers of `queue_strategic()` anywhere are unit tests and the `tests/manual/`
  sim harness.
- The queue the player can actually SEE is `GameState.queued_actions`, filled by
  `GameManager.select_action()`, which charges Attention by incrementing `attention_spent`
  directly and never mints a `queued_strategic` entry.

So in the shipped game the "pull from planned work" option can never pull from planned
work -- its WIP registry has no producer, and the visible queue is invisible to it. The
refusal explained a budget where the truth was an absence. Pip's instinct was exactly
right: it isn't strictly true.

(`QueueGantt.rows_from_state()` renders `queued_strategic` as the "strategic WIP" lane of
the on-screen gantt, so that lane is also always empty. The player's planned work shows up
only via the separate "planned" tentative rows.)

## The convention

Implemented in the linked PR; recorded here because the convention outlives the fix.

Every refusal is exactly one of two kinds, and the code must say which:

| kind | meaning | ships as |
|---|---|---|
| **RULE** | a real game constraint | the sentence, unmarked |
| **STUB** | refuses because the behaviour is unbuilt | the sentence + Pip's `[ALPHA: ...]` marker |

There is deliberately **no third constructor**. A refusal that states a reason which is not
the actual reason ("WRONG") is a defect to fix at the call site, not a category to ship.

### Why it should resist rot

The `_facts_this_copy_must_not_break` block rotted because it relied on remembering. Three
independent properties here do not:

1. **The classification is a required choice, not a remembered step.** `Refusal.rule()` and
   `Refusal.stub()` are the only constructors. There is no unclassified one to fall into.
2. **The marker expires on its own.** It is gated on `BuildInfo.ALPHA_TOOLS_ERA` -- the
   existing era switch already documented "flip false at 1.0". No stub marker can survive
   into the finished game by being forgotten; one flip retires all of them.
3. **A ratchet, not a plea.** `tools/check_refusal_classification.py` fails any refusal that
   is neither classified nor in `tools/refusal_baseline.txt`, and that baseline may only
   shrink. New debt cannot be added silently; and because the baseline is keyed on the
   message text, *rewording* an old refusal knocks it out of the baseline too -- touching an
   old lie makes you classify it.

Plus a fourth, specific to the fix: the cannibalize discriminator is **derived, not
declared**. It classifies as STUB exactly when nothing was cannibalisable, so the day
anyone wires `queue_strategic_action()` into the UI, the marker retires itself and the
genuine RULE takes over. Nobody has to remember to switch it off. `test_refusal_stub_vs_rule.gd`
pins both halves.

### It extends prior art rather than competing with it

Searched first. Three existing half-conventions, now subsumed rather than paralleled:

- `is_stub: true` + `[Coming Soon]` in `godot/data/actions/travel.json`, consumed by
  `travel_panel_controller.gd`. That marks an **action** as unbuilt *before* the player
  presses. `Refusal` marks a **refusal** as unbuilt *after* they press. Different moments,
  both wanted. (This is `TECH_DEBT_BURNDOWN.md` item 5, open pending a keep-vs-hide ruling.)
- `ALPHA_TOOLS_TOGGLE_WARNING` / `ALPHA_TOOLS_GAME_OVER_NOTICE` in `game_config.gd` -- the
  settled wording for dev powers. Same era switch, same ASCII bracket chrome, different
  subject.
- `BuildInfo.ALPHA_TOOLS_ERA` -- reused as the expiry gate rather than inventing a second
  era switch.

## Open follow-ups this convention exposes but does not close

1. **The option label is still a promise the game cannot keep.** `hiring_pipeline.gd` offers
   "Set them up now (N Att, pull from planned work)" and "Mentor them (N Att, pull from
   planned work)". Marking the refusal stops the lie at the moment of refusal; the *offer*
   still names a mechanic with no producer. That needs a rewrite, not a correction, and the
   copy is Pip's -- proposed, not done.
2. **The real fix is to build it, or to remove the verb.** Either wire
   `queue_strategic_action()` into the plan screen so "planned work" means the queue the
   player sees, or collapse the two HANDLE verbs to one until it does.
3. **`advertise` is greyed "SOON" on the action bar while the same mechanic ships enabled
   one panel away** (`action_bar_renderer.gd` `COMING_SOON_ACTION_IDS` vs
   `hiring_panel_controller.gd`). The refusal is false: it refuses because of a hardcoded
   list, not because the feature is missing. Behaviour change, needs a design call.
4. **`employee_screen.gd` delivers a refusal to a method that does not exist**
   (`game_manager.has_method("add_message")` is false), so confirming "Fire" with
   insufficient severance closes the dialog and says nothing at all. A silent refusal is the
   limit case of this whole issue.
5. **`DESIGN_PHILOSOPHY.md` cannot currently be committed to.** The matching entry for its
   "On honesty and legibility" section was written and then reverted: the file carries 185
   pre-existing non-ASCII characters (85 em-dashes, 81 arrows, 14 ellipses) and the
   BLOCKING `enforce-standards` pre-commit hook rejects it on line 1. Editing the doc where
   design principles are supposed to be recorded therefore requires either a 185-character
   sweep of Pip's prose or `--no-verify`. That is its own anti-rot failure and wants its own
   decision (sweep it, or exempt legacy docs), so it is reported rather than papered over.

6. **The guard covers one shape only.** It detects the `{"success": false, ...}` Dictionary
   form. Bare rejection strings (`error_occurred.emit(...)`, UI labels, disabled-button
   tooltips) are audited by hand and not gated. Stated in the tool's docstring so nobody
   trusts it further than it goes.

issues.title: Attention spent without saying so: the 4 surfaces PR #1217 could not fix display-only, + the cat has no art SLOT (not a missing asset)

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
Follow-up to PR #1217, which fixed the reported case (the stray cat) and its whole
class (all 25 popup events). This is everything the same audit found that could
**not** be fixed display-only, filed together rather than as five thin issues.

The audit worked from the code, not the UI: every path that reaches
`MonthPlan.spend_attention()` / `can_spend_hours()` / `pay_by_cannibalizing()`,
traced back to what triggers it.

## Full audit result

Ranked by how likely a player is to hit it.

| # | Surface | Attention | Shown before commit? | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Popup events / response windows** (25 events, 75 options -- incl. the stray cat) | 1 (`DEFAULT_ATTENTION_COST`) | **HIDDEN** -- and hidden after, too | **FIXED in #1217** |
| 2 | Action bar + icon-grid submenus (fundraising / publicity / strategic / operations / financing) | 1-2, declared in `costs` | SHOWN -- on-face cost label + tooltip + hover info bar | OK |
| 3 | Direct-hire actions (`hiring.json`, 7 of them) | 1, declared | SHOWN | OK |
| 4 | **Hiring action-bar entries** (`advertise`, `use_connections`, `interview_next`, `hire_best`, `onboard_next`) | 3 / 2 / 2 / 1 / 1-2 each | **HIDDEN -- actively labelled "No costs"** | **Below, item A** |
| 5 | Hiring **panel** buttons (same five actions, different surface) | same | SHOWN on the button face | OK -- but see item A |
| 6 | **Conference trip** (travel submenu -> commit dialog) | **all remaining**, re-charged per month boundary while away | **tile says "Free"**; commit button says "all remaining Attention" but no number | **Below, item B** |
| 7 | Audit action (`operations.json`) | 1, `audits` kind | SHOWN | OK |
| 8 | `#789` hiring accept-prompt windows | 1-2 | SHOWN -- price *and* payment source in the option text | OK |
| 9 | Ledger attention-denominated bill | `entry.principal` | AUTOMATIC (no click) | **Below, item C** |
| 10 | `MediaSystem.execute_exclusive_interview` | 1 | UNREACHABLE -- zero callers | **Below, item D** |

**Counts: 1 HIDDEN fixed, 2 HIDDEN outstanding (items A and B), 1 automatic, 1
dead, 5 already correct.** Nothing landed in SHOWN LATE except the conference
trip's numeric figure, which appears post-commit in the vignette and the return
backlog panel.

---

## A. Five hiring actions print "No costs" and spend 1-3 Attention

`godot/data/actions/core.json` -- `advertise`, `use_connections`,
`interview_next`, `hire_best`, `onboard_next` all declare `"costs": {}`. The
hover info bar therefore renders `[color=gray]No costs[/color]`
(`main_ui.gd:2174`), and `action_bar_renderer`'s affordability check never greys
them out. They are not merely unlabelled -- they are **labelled free**.

What they actually spend, via `HiringPipeline`:

| action | Attention | source |
|---|---|---|
| `advertise` | 3 | `hiring.advertise.cost_attention` |
| `use_connections` | 2 | `hiring.connections.cost_attention` |
| `interview_next` | 2 | `hiring.interview.cost_attention` |
| `hire_best` | 1 | `hiring.offer.cost_attention` |
| `onboard_next` | 1-2 **per hire**, one click | `HiringPipeline.ONBOARD_ATTENTION` |

`onboard_next` is the sharp one: a single click auto-picks the next step for
*every* hire in flight, so with three hires cooking it can drain 3-6 Attention
with no number anywhere.

**Why this is not a data edit.** Putting `"attention": 3` into `advertise`'s
`costs` would **double-charge** -- `game_manager.gd:218-275` debits declared
Attention at queue time, and the pipeline debits again at execution time. The
`costs: {}` is load-bearing. This needs a display-only channel (the same shape as
#1217's stamp), not a JSON change.

Note the same five actions are already correct on the *hiring panel*, which puts
"Advertise\n($8k + 3 Att)" on the button face -- so the game shows the price on
one surface and denies it on another. Also worth a look while in there: those
panel labels are **hardcoded literals**, not read from `Balance`, so a retune
desyncs them silently. Two of the five (`systems`, `meet_people`) do read the
constant; the rest do not.

`hiring_panel_controller.gd` also uses none of the three shared cost helpers
(`_format_costs_inline`, `_costs_affordable`, `_make_cost_label`) that
`submenu_controller.gd` and `travel_panel_controller.gd` both use, and has no
cost-based affordability gating at all -- clicking with insufficient Attention
runs the delegate and surfaces a red log line after the fact.

## B. The conference trip tile says "Free"

`travel.json` -> `attend_conference_trip` has `"costs": {}` with a `_seam`
comment explaining why (the trip resolves synchronously at commit time, not
through the plan queue). Consequence:
`main_ui._format_costs_inline({})` returns `"Free"`, and the travel submenu
renders that on the tile face.

What it actually costs (`conference_trip.gd:280-286`): **every un-reserved
OPERATING hour you have left** --

```gdscript
var free: int = mini(
    state.month_plan.hours_available(MonthPlan.HOUR_OPERATING),
    state.month_plan.available()
)
```

-- and it is charged **again at every month boundary crossed while away**
(`conference_trip.gd:180`), so the fresh grant of the new month is wiped too.
That repeat drain is disclosed nowhere in the UI, only in a docstring.
`can_commit()` checks money only, never Attention.

The commit button is honest but non-numeric ("Commit -- $X + all remaining
Attention"). The tile that leads to it is the problem. A fix wants either a
display override on the tile or a projected figure on the commit button; the
number does exist at commit time.

Deliberately not attempted in #1217: it needs `main_ui.gd` /
`submenu_controller.gd`, both live in concurrent lanes this week.

## C. The ledger's attention bill has no cause-log entry

`ledger.gd:280-288` bills `int(e.principal)` OPERATING hours during
`tick_and_bill()`. It is the **only** currency branch in that switch that does not
call `_note(...)`, so it produces no `cause_log` attribution -- the player would
see the hours vanish with a single feed line and no trace in the breakdown.

Low urgency: **no live producer mints an attention-denominated entry today.**
Every factory (`Ledger.loan`, `funding_strings`, `desperation_payroll`,
`staff_rider`, `appetite_promise`, `FinanceEngine._standing_rider`,
`WindowResolver._mint_deferral`) mints money / governance / papers / compute /
equity. The branch is reachable only via `Ledger.from_dict` rehydration. Worth
fixing before anything starts minting them, not after.

## D. `MediaSystem` is dead code

`MediaSystem.execute_exclusive_interview` (`media_system.gd:232-246`) spends 1
OPERATING hour and has **zero callers**. The class is never instantiated,
`GameState` has no `media_system` member, and no `exclusive_interview` action id
exists in `godot/data/`. Only two comments reference it. Either wire it with a
declared cost or delete it -- as written, re-wiring it as-is would ship another
hidden charge (its only Attention disclosure is a rejection string).

---

## E. Separate, and a different owner: the stray cat renders with no art

Reported in the same playtest: *"Stray cat appearing doesn't have any graphics on
it yet despite having assets in the queue."*

**Verdict: neither a missing-asset problem nor an unpromoted-asset problem.**
It is a third thing, and it matters because it means neither the art owner nor
`#1166`'s share-set route can fix it.

**There is no slot to promote art INTO.** Three independent checks:

1. **No art field exists on the event schema.** Union of every key used across all
   25 events in `godot/data/events/core_events.json`: `id`, `name`, `description`,
   `type`, `trigger_type`, `trigger_turn`, `trigger_condition`, `repeatable`,
   `options`, `probability`, `min_turn`, `cooldown_turns`, `extra_condition`.
   Option level: `id`, `text`, `costs`, `effects`, `message`. No image, icon,
   texture, art or portrait key anywhere.
2. **The presenter cannot render one.** `godot/scripts/ui/event_dialog.gd` is 497
   lines and builds its panel entirely in code. It contains **zero** matches for
   `texture|sprite|image|.png|.svg|.jpg` -- there is no `TextureRect` in the
   dialog at all.
3. **The demand manifest is empty.** ADR-0019 makes packing demand-gated ("the
   only path into `godot/assets/` is a mechanically verified demand entry"), and
   `tools/assets/demand/slot_picks.json` currently has `"slots": {}`. There is no
   demand entry that could pull a cat into an event popup, and none could be
   written, because there is no slot.

Meanwhile the art is not the constraint. Cat art is abundant in `art_source/`
(eight-plus pixellab cat directories) and some is **already packed**:
`godot/assets/cats/simple/` holds 8 live photos and `assets/images/office_cat.png`
is referenced by `main.tscn`. But that art belongs to the **office cat widget**
(`office_cat.gd`, the persistent decoration + credits surface), which is a
different consumer from the encounter.

So the owner here is **engineering, not art**: an art channel on the event popup
(schema field + a `TextureRect` in `event_dialog.gd` + a demand slot) has to exist
*before* promotion is even a question. Filed here as the finding; no art was
touched.

---

Audit method, so it can be re-run: start from `grep -rn "spend_attention\|can_spend_hours\|pay_by_cannibalizing"`
over `godot/scripts/`, then trace each site back to its trigger and forward to its
presenting UI.

issues.title: Half-day workshop: the first ten turns -- a first-timer could not tell what to do, and 44 -> 87 proves the surface is responsive, not that it is finished

labels.name: strategic
labels.description: Strategic planning and high-level architectural decisions

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
**Pip, 2026-08-12: *"make a note that we need to workshop the first ten turns of
the game probably pretty soon."***

This is a request for a **design session**, not a fix. Filing it as an issue so
it exists as a schedulable thing rather than a sentence in a memo, in the same
format as **#984** (*"Half-day workshop: audit mechanics deep-dive"*).

The rest of this issue is the context that has to walk into the room, because
scattered across a playtest file, an issue and a handover it does not add up to
the thing it adds up to together.

## The observation that started it

A real first-time player, given the shipped build for 27 minutes on 2026-08-10,
**could not work out what to do.**

Recorded flatly in `coordination/DESIGN_2026-08-12_interrupt-resolution-variants.md:64`,
inside an argument about a *different* feature -- which is what makes it worth
quoting, because it is being used as a load-bearing constraint rather than as a
complaint:

> The honest risk: it asks a new player to schedule before they understand what any of the actions do. **Jason could not tell what to do at all.** This adds a dimension on top of that.

That session is written up in `coordination/PLAYTEST_2026-08-10_jason.md`. It also
produced the first external evidence the global leaderboard works end to end: his
run went up as **44 turns**, fifth on the board.

## What landed since, and exactly what it proves

The first-five-minutes work merged this week. `main` now carries PLAN-phase
rejections that actually reach the player and a legible turn one. The direct
cause was **#1202**, which found the sharpest instance and measured it: the
confirmation messages were written to a node that is `visible = false` throughout
PLAN, and the game opens in PLAN, so **26 of 33 `log_message()` call sites in
`main_ui.gd` fired into an invisible log.** A player clicking an action they could
not afford saw nothing happen at all. Not skippable -- invisible.

Then: **a real first-time player scored 87, against 44 on Monday**
(`coordination/HANDOVER_2026-08-13_alsobort-state.md:76`), on the public board,
outbox drained.

**Read that number carefully, because it is the reason for the workshop and not a
reason against it.**

- It is **one run by one player**, and the handover does not establish that it is
  the *same* player as the 44. Treat it as a signal, not a controlled comparison.
- What it does show is that **the early game is responsive to small legibility
  fixes** -- roughly a doubling of turns survived from making existing feedback
  visible. Nothing was added. Something already there was un-hidden.
- **What it does not show is that the first ten turns are finished.** A surface
  that doubles when you stop hiding your own error messages is a surface that had
  a long way to come, not one that has arrived. The measurement establishes
  headroom, not completion.

**That distinction is the whole argument for a workshop rather than more
patches.** Patches are what produced 44 -> 87, and they worked. The question a
patch cannot answer is what the first ten turns are *for*.

## Why ten turns, and why a workshop

**Ten turns is the unit the game is actually judged in.** It is roughly the
27-minute session that Jason had and the length of any friend-link trial. If a
player cannot form a plan by turn ten, nothing later in the design is ever
reached.

**The known problems are not independent bugs -- they interlock, which is what a
workshop is for and a patch queue is not.** From #1202 and the playtest, all in
the same ten turns:

1. Feedback was invisible; now visible, but never designed -- it was never
   decided *what* turn one should confirm, only that it should confirm something.
2. Scouting actions have **no icons**, so an unlabelled tile that also produced no
   confirmation was indistinguishable from a dead button (#1202, item 2).
3. **Actions resolve instantly, so the early game has no rhythm** (#1044) -- there
   is nothing for the confirmation to be a confirmation *of*.
4. The vocabulary a new player meets in those turns is undefined: founder hour
   kinds (#1208) and league seed / board key (#1209) are both terms of art shown
   to players with no player-facing definition.
5. The narrative cold-open and first-turn direction have been open since the
   first playtest (#801: *"lots of info, not a lot of direction"*).

Each has been picked at individually for weeks. **The reason they persist is that
each one's fix is partly someone else's problem.** Deciding what turn one teaches
determines what needs confirming, which determines what needs pacing, which
determines what needs naming. That is one conversation, held once.

## The caution that belongs in the room

From `coordination/DESIGN_2026-08-10_calendar-and-persistent-stage.md:203`, written
by the seat that ran the session:

> This is a large design surface assembled from a single 27-minute session with one player. **Jason is one data point, he is a friend, and he was being shown the game rather than left alone with it.** The readability and confirmation findings are almost certainly general.

So: the *legibility* findings generalise and have now been partly confirmed by a
second player's score. **Anything the workshop concludes about what the first ten
turns should teach is not yet evidence-backed** and should be built to be tested,
not shipped as settled. A concrete output worth asking for is a way to run the
next first-timer **unattended** -- Jason was guided, and that is the one variable
neither data point controls for.

## Scheduling -- and the constraint this issue must name

`coordination/PLAN_2026-08-13_manifund-runway-daybyday.md:148` says:

> **Kill for now:** anything needing a workshop that has not been scheduled by Mon 17. There is no room for a multi-day session that produces ADRs before the freeze.

**That rule does not exclude this; it dates it.** Two honest options, and the
choice is Pip's:

- **Schedule it by Mon 17** as a **half-day**, matching #984's shape -- not a
  multi-day ADR-producing session. The first ten turns are also the thing a
  Manifund reviewer would open the build and see, so the case for it being inside
  the runway rather than after it is real.
- **Or park it explicitly for after 9 Sep**, and say so here, so it is deferred
  rather than quietly dropped.

What must not happen is the third thing: the surface keeps improving by patch,
the number keeps going up, and the question of what the opening is *for* never
gets asked because it never had a date.

## Suggested shape, if it is held

Half a day. Inputs: the #1202 findings, `PLAYTEST_2026-08-10_jason.md`, and both
runs. Outputs, in order of what the other issues are blocked on:

1. **What must a player be able to do, and believe, by turn 10?** One paragraph.
   Everything else follows from it.
2. **Turn one specifically** -- what it teaches, what it confirms, what it must
   not show yet.
3. **Which of the five interlocking items above are consequences of (1)** and can
   therefore be closed or re-scoped rather than fixed as filed.
4. **How the next first-timer is run unattended**, so turn 11 of this
   conversation has evidence instead of a third anecdote.

## Related

- **#1202** -- early-game legibility, five findings; the measured cause of the
  invisible-feedback defect. **The main input.**
- **#801** -- onboarding: narrative cold-open + first-turn direction. Open since
  playtest #1; the oldest statement of this problem.
- **#1044** -- design(tempo): actions resolve instantly, so the early game has no
  rhythm.
- **#722** -- opt-in Tutorial Mode. A candidate answer, which should not be
  assumed to be *the* answer before (1) above is decided.
- **#1125** -- GO: retime first; the turn-pacing premise.
- **#1208 / #1209** -- undefined player-facing vocabulary encountered in these
  same turns.
- **#984** -- the precedent for this format.

issues.title: input(dev): ESC/pause disables ALL diagnostic surfaces -- root cause is process_mode, not input priority

labels.name: ux
labels.description: What happens when you use it. If a fix needs new behaviour or words, it is ux.

issues.body:
Raised by Pip while playtesting 2026-07-30, verbatim:

> "esc menu seems to override dev menu, maybe those should have different overall weight? dev should probably override everything so can diagnose / bug report / issues etc with menus?"

The design ask is right. The mechanism is NOT the one the symptom suggests, so this
was investigated before proposing a fix.

## What is actually happening (CONFIRMED from source)

The operative mechanism is `process_mode`, not input handling order.

1. `godot/scripts/ui/pause_menu.gd:87` -- `show_pause_menu()` does
   `get_tree().paused = true`.
2. `godot/scenes/pause_menu.tscn:19` -- `process_mode = 3`
   (`PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`). The pause menu is the only surface in the frame
   deliberately exempted from the pause it just caused.
3. `godot/autoload/keybind_manager.gd:280` `_input()` is where BOTH diagnostic
   surfaces are actually dispatched from:
   - `:301-303` `debug_overlay` (F3) -> `debug_overlay_toggled.emit()`
   - `:306-308` `dev_mode` (backslash) -> `dev_mode_toggled.emit()`
   Neither `godot/scripts/debug/dev_mode_overlay.gd` nor
   `godot/scripts/debug/debug_overlay.gd` defines an `_input()` of its own --
   grep confirms zero `_input` / `_unhandled_input` in either file. The dev
   overlay subscribes to the signal at `dev_mode_overlay.gd:56`.
4. `KeybindManager` is an autoload (`godot/project.godot` `[autoload]`) with **no
   `process_mode` override**. Grep over `godot/autoload/*.gd` finds exactly two
   files that set one -- `leaderboard_sync.gd:49` and `update_check.gd:67`, both
   `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`. KeybindManager inherits, i.e. pausable.

INFERRED (not verified by running the game, which is out of scope while main is
frozen): therefore, the instant the pause menu opens, `KeybindManager._input()`
stops being called at all, and **every global hotkey dies -- backslash, F3, F6
flight recorder, F7 UI-evolution shot, screenshot, log export**. The
`get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` at `pause_menu.gd:94` is a red herring:
it fires only inside the `KEY_ESCAPE and visible` branch, so it consumes ESC and
nothing else.

The converse direction Pip actually observed has the same root:
`godot/scripts/ui/main_ui.gd:498-505` opens the pause menu on ESC with no test
for whether the dev overlay is open (it cannot test -- the overlay has no input
claim). So ESC with the dev overlay up pauses the tree underneath it. The
overlay stays *visible* (a CanvasLayer keeps drawing) but its dev-poke Buttons go
dead, because `main_ui.gd:326-328` adds it as a child of MainUI, which is
pausable. `DebugOverlay` (`godot/scenes/main.tscn:416`) is likewise a child of
the pausable main scene root. That is exactly "esc menu overrides dev menu".

Secondary, INFERRED, and *not* the operative cause here: Godot dispatches
`_input` in reverse tree order, so the main scene's nodes are polled before
autoloads added earlier at the root. A scene-level `set_input_as_handled()` can
therefore pre-empt KeybindManager in the unpaused case. Worth knowing, but no
current binding collides.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than shrugging at

Pip's stated reason is the whole point: the pause menu is the one state you reach
when something looks wrong, and it is precisely the state in which you can no
longer read the dev readout, take a flight-recorder snapshot, or grab a
screenshot for a bug report. The diagnostic layer is disabled exactly when it is
needed. Same family as #1027's "silent wrongness" thesis, one step removed: the
instrument does not report anything false, it just silently stops existing.

## Options

**A. Elevate KeybindManager only (one line).**
`process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` in `keybind_manager.gd:_ready()`.
Hotkeys keep firing while paused. Cheapest. Incomplete: the overlays would
toggle visibility but their buttons stay unclickable, and it also un-pauses
screenshot/log-export/admin binds, which is probably desirable but is a wider
blast radius than "dev diagnostics".

**B. Elevate KeybindManager AND both overlays.** A plus
`PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` on `DevModeOverlay` (set in `dev_mode_overlay.gd:_ready()`
next to the existing `layer = OVERLAY_LAYER` at `:46`) and on the `DebugOverlay`
node. Delivers the actual ask -- diagnose *while* paused, buttons live. This is
my recommendation. Note the dev overlay's pokes mutate GameManager state while
the tree is paused; that is fine for a dev build (the pokes are already arbitrary
state edits) but should be a conscious call, not a side effect.

**C. Split the binds.** Give the DEBUG-category binds their own always-processing
dispatcher and leave gameplay binds pausable. Cleanest conceptually, most code,
and `keybind_manager.gd` already has a `Category.DEBUG` to key off. Overkill for
now; worth it if the always-on set later needs to differ from "all of them".

**D. Also make ESC yield when a dev surface is open.** Independent of A-C: have
`main_ui.gd:498-505` decline to open the pause menu if the dev overlay is
visible, so ESC closes the dev overlay first (standard LIFO). #1002 landed a
shared `ModalStack` chokepoint for exactly this kind of LIFO ordering -- the dev
overlay is currently outside it. Judgement call: if B lands, D matters much less,
because the overlay would remain usable under the pause menu anyway.

Not proposing a mandate. B+D is what I would pick; B alone gets 80% of the value
for one line each.

## Scope note

Dev-build-only surfaces (`BuildInfo.is_dev_build()` gates `dev_mode_overlay.gd:48`),
so nothing here changes the shipping player build. NOT league-blocking for Friday.
It does slow down every playtest bug report between now and then, which is the
real cost.

Related: #1002 (ModalStack LIFO chokepoint), #1011 (three docs disagree with
`keybind_manager.gd`), #1027.

issues.title: dev+ux: no way to replay the cold-open intro -- add a reset for last_seen_intro_version

issues.body:
Pip needs to replay the cold-open repeatedly while playtesting. Today there is no
in-game way to do that -- once seen, it is seen forever.

## Evidence (CONFIRMED)

- `godot/autoload/game_config.gd:110` -- `var last_seen_intro_version: String = ""`
  (`"" = never seen the cold-open`), persisted in the config `game` section.
- `godot/autoload/game_config.gd:151` -- `const INTRO_VERSION: String = "1"`,
  deliberately independent of `CURRENT_VERSION` so ordinary patches do not
  re-trigger the intro.
- `godot/autoload/game_config.gd:535-544` -- the whole gate:
  ```
  func should_show_intro() -> bool:
      if not play_intros:
          return false
      return last_seen_intro_version != INTRO_VERSION
  ```

So a reset is: set `last_seen_intro_version = ""` and `save_config()`. That is
the entire change. Nothing else reads the field. No migration, no versioning
concern, no ladder impact (this is presentation state, not run state).

Note the gate is already deliberately clean -- the comment at `:530-533` records
that it is gated PURELY on `last_seen_intro_version` and NOT on `games_played`,
specifically to be immune to the `increment_games_played()` ordering in
`config_confirmation.gd`. Whoever wrote #801 left this easy on purpose.

## Manual workaround for today (no code change)

Edit the persisted config and blank the value, then relaunch:

- Windows user config path is Godot's `user://` --
  `%APPDATA%/Godot/app_userdata/<project name>/` (the project name comes from
  `godot/project.godot`). Find the config file written by
  `GameConfig.save_config()`, locate the `game` section's
  `last_seen_intro_version`, set it to an empty string, save.

Setting it to any string other than `"1"` also works -- the gate is an
inequality, not an emptiness test. `play_intros` must also be true.

## Where should the control live? (options, not a mandate)

**A. Dev overlay button.** `godot/scripts/debug/dev_mode_overlay.gd` already
hosts a column of dev "pokes". A `Replay Intro` button there is the smallest,
lowest-risk change, ships in dev builds only, and directly serves the stated need
(Pip replaying it while playtesting). Downside: does nothing for players, and it
inherits the pause-interaction problem filed separately in the ESC/dev-overlay
issue.

**B. Settings menu entry.** `godot/scenes/settings_menu.tscn` +
`settings_menu.gd`, next to the existing `play_intros` toggle. Player-visible
("Replay intro"), which is a genuinely nice thing to have -- players who skipped
the cold-open on first run currently cannot ever see it. Downside: player-facing
UI change during a release freeze, needs a string and a layout slot.

**C. Both.** B for players, A for the tight playtest loop.

Recommendation: **A now** (dev-only, zero player-build risk, unblocks Pip's loop
this week), **B queued for after the Friday cut** as a small UX win. Do not do B
before the freeze lifts.

Either way, implement it as a single named function on GameConfig
(`reset_intro_seen()`) so both call sites share it and the field is not poked
from UI code.

## Size

Genuinely tiny -- one function on GameConfig plus one button. Filing it because
it is easy to lose, not because it is hard.

Related: #801 (the cold-open intro gate this reverses), #1028 (the pause/dev-overlay interaction referenced above).
